entries.summary: Scheduler: month, week and day event layout, editing, range selection, custom headers and context menus.
Surface: the base surface (background + shadow tokens) other components sit on.
Card with Header, Title, Description, Content and Footer parts.
Separator on the cdk Separator (hr, or a vertical role=separator).
Header: section header text on the cdk Header.
Label on the cdk Label, with required / invalid / disabled modifiers.
Description: field help text (cdk Text, slot description).
ErrorMessage: field error text (cdk Text, slot errorMessage).
FieldError: a field's validation errors, shown while invalid (cdk FieldError).
Kbd: keyboard keys and shortcuts, with key symbols and names.
Spinner: a loading indicator (role=status).
Skeleton: a loading placeholder with shimmer or pulse.
EmptyState: a placeholder for empty lists and searches; optional media, title, description and actions parts.
DataGrid: a data-driven grid with sorting, selection, resizing, pinning, tree rows, reordering and virtualization (Rivet addition on @rivetjs/cdk/data-grid).
Carousel: a slide show with buttons, dots, thumbnails, autoplay and drag (Rivet addition on @rivetjs/cdk/carousel).
Lightbox: a full-screen viewer for images, video, embeds and PDF with zoom, captions, thumbnails and more (Rivet addition on @rivetjs/cdk/lightbox).
Badge: a count or status marker pinned to a corner of its anchor.
Chip: a small inline label with color, size and variant.
Alert: a status message with Indicator, Content, Title and Description parts.
Typography: the type scale (Heading, Paragraph, Code, Prose).
Link on the cdk Link, with an optional trailing icon.
Button on the cdk Button: variants, sizes, icon-only, render props.
ButtonGroup: buttons sharing size, variant and disabled state (cdk Group).
ToggleButton on the cdk ToggleButton (aria-pressed, two-way isSelected).
ToggleButtonGroup on the cdk ToggleButtonGroup (single or multiple selection, arrow keys).
Segment (Rivet addition): segmented control on the cdk ToggleButtonGroup (single selection) with a gliding SelectionIndicator.
CloseButton: an icon-only close button on the cdk Button.
Avatar: an image with a fallback, on a port of the Radix avatar primitive.
AvatarGroup: stacked avatars with a max and a +N count.
ProgressBar on the cdk ProgressBar (determinate or indeterminate).
ProgressCircle: a circular progress indicator on the cdk ProgressBar.
Meter on the cdk Meter (role=meter).

Resizable (Rivet addition): shadcn/ui ResizablePanelGroup / ResizablePanel / ResizableHandle (+ ResizableIndicator, handle types line / drag / pill / handle, separator-token variants) on the cdk resizable, Rivet UI look.
ScrollArea (Rivet addition): Radix ScrollArea behaviour from the cdk with overlay scrollbars, sizes, variants and a ScrollShadow fade.
ScrollShadow: fades the scrolled-away edges of a scroll container (CSS scroll-driven, attribute fallback).
Popover: Trigger, Content, Dialog, Heading and Arrow on the cdk DialogTrigger / Popover / Dialog.
Tooltip: Trigger, Content and Arrow on the cdk TooltipTrigger / Tooltip (hover + focus, warmup).
Input: single-line text input on the cdk Input (primary / secondary, full width; TextField variant).
TextArea: multiline text input on the cdk TextArea (primary / secondary, full width; TextField variant).
TextField on the cdk TextField: label, Input / TextArea, description, field error; variant context.
Form on the cdk Form (validation behaviour, server errors).
Fieldset with Legend, Group and Actions parts; a disabled fieldset disables the cdk components inside.
Breadcrumbs: Item links on the cdk Breadcrumbs / Breadcrumb (current page, separators).
Toolbar: container of controls with arrow-key navigation on the cdk Toolbar.
ActionBar (Rivet addition): floating bottom toolbar for bulk actions on a selection; Prefix (live count), Content, Suffix on the ui Toolbar.
Morph (Rivet addition): a pill that morphs into a panel and back (house motion, eight directions, primary / secondary), focus in and back, Escape / outside close.
ItemMorph (Rivet addition): iOS-style item preview — a ListBox / GridList / Menu item lifts into a panel on a long press, right click, press or Shift+F10 and morphs back.
Rating (Rivet addition): star (or any lucide icon) rating on native radios, or a read-only fractional display; render function per item.
TrendChip (Rivet addition): direction of a change with a lucide icon and a good / bad colour (inverted for lower-is-better), prefix / suffix, custom indicator.
Kpi (Rivet addition): metric card with title, icon, formatted value, trend, progress, description, chart, actions and footer slots.
CellSwitch (Rivet addition): a settings-row switch; the whole row toggles.
HoverCard (Rivet addition): a preview card on hover, keyboard focus or long press.
EmojiReactionButton (Rivet addition): an emoji + count reaction toggle, sizes, read-only.
ContextMenu (Rivet addition): a right-click / long-press menu at the pointer on the Dropdown parts.
Command (Rivet addition): a modal command palette; search field filtering grouped commands, sizes, backdrops.
ListView (Rivet addition): a single-column interactive list on GridList (variants, selection checkboxes, row actions, empty state, virtualization).
FileTree (Rivet addition): a file / folder tree on Tree (sizes, guide lines, icons, custom indicator, selection).
PressableFeedback (Rivet addition): a pressable with highlight, ripple, hold-to-confirm and progress feedback layers.
HoloCard (Rivet addition): a 3D tilting card with a pointer-tracked holographic glare (CSS variables, CSS tilt).
FloatingToc (Rivet addition): section bars that open a floating list of sections on hover or press.
CellColorPicker (Rivet addition): a settings-row ColorPicker (label, hex value, swatch, popover).
DropZone (Rivet addition): a drag-and-drop / paste / browse upload area with a file list (format badge, progress, retry, remove).
KpiGroup (Rivet addition): KPI cards on one shared surface, horizontal or vertical, with separators.
NumberValue (Rivet addition): locale-aware formatted number (currency, percent, unit, compact, sign) with prefix / suffix.
Widget (Rivet addition): dashboard container with header, legend, raised content area and footer.
DescriptionList (Rivet addition): key / value rows (order summaries, totals, specs) with an emphasized total row.
FeatureList (Rivet addition): perks / plan features with a leading lucide icon (check by default).
Status (Rivet addition): status / presence / unread dot in the semantic colours, three sizes, optional CSS pulse.
ItemCard (Rivet addition): list row card with icon, title, description and a trailing action.
ItemCardGroup (Rivet addition): item cards as a divided list or a grid, with a section header.
Timeline (Rivet addition): read-only chronology on a start or centred rail with status markers.
Charts (Rivet addition): area, line, bar (grouped, stacked, horizontal), donut and sparkline charts rendered on the server, gaps for missing values, dots, CSS-only tooltips.
ChartTooltip (Rivet addition): tooltip parts (header, items, indicator, label, value) for custom chart tooltips.
PieChart (Rivet addition): pie and donut rings rendered on the server with labels, legend and CSS-only tooltips.
RadarChart (Rivet addition): polygon or circle grid radar with one or more series, server-rendered.
RadialChart (Rivet addition): concentric progress rings with track, legend and centre content.
ComposedChart (Rivet addition): bar, line and area series on one cartesian frame.
Kanban (Rivet addition): board of columns and draggable cards on cdk DropList / Drag, with createKanban state.
Navbar (Rivet addition): responsive top bar with brand, items, mobile menu, zero-JS hide on scroll and router integration.
Sidebar (Rivet addition): the shadcn/ui Sidebar parts from @rivetjs/cdk/sidebar with the Rivet UI look; collapsible, cookie-persisted, a swipeable sheet on mobile.
AppLayout (Rivet addition): app shell of sidebar, sticky navbar, main, aside, toolbar and footer; resizable, persisted panels and a mobile aside sheet.
Masonry + Bento (Rivet additions): masonry columns and span tiles on @rivetjs/cdk/masonry; server-exact placement, measured / virtualized modes, keys, selection.
Compare (Rivet addition): before / after layers with a draggable divider (round handle, labels) on @rivetjs/cdk/compare; keys, drag anywhere, vertical.
Stepper (Rivet addition): progress through numbered steps with indicators, titles, descriptions and separators on @rivetjs/cdk/stepper.
Modal: Trigger, Backdrop, Container, Dialog, Header, Icon, Heading, Body, Footer and CloseTrigger on the cdk DialogTrigger / ModalOverlay / Modal / Dialog; useOverlayState.
InputGroup with Prefix, Input, TextArea and Suffix parts on the cdk Group.
SearchField with Group, SearchIcon, Input and ClearButton parts on the cdk SearchField.
NumberField with Group, Input, IncrementButton and DecrementButton parts on the cdk NumberField.
NumberStepper (Rivet addition): pill stepper on the cdk NumberField; Group, Value (animated display), Decrement / Increment buttons.
ListBox: options with an item indicator and sections on the cdk ListBox.
ListBoxItem: an option of a ListBox (+ Indicator) on the cdk ListBoxItem.
ListBoxSection: a group of ListBox options on the cdk ListBoxSection.
Tag: a tag of a TagGroup with an optional remove button, on the cdk Tag.
TagGroup: a focusable, selectable list of tags on the cdk TagGroup / TagList.
AlertDialog: Trigger, Backdrop, Container, Dialog (role alertdialog), Header, Heading, Body, Footer, Icon (status) and CloseTrigger on the cdk DialogTrigger / ModalOverlay / Modal / Dialog.

Drawer: Trigger, Backdrop, Content (placement), Dialog (drag to dismiss on cdk motion), Header, Heading, Body, Footer, Handle and CloseTrigger on the cdk DialogTrigger / ModalOverlay / Modal / Dialog.
Sheet (Rivet addition): draggable edge sheet with snap points, nested and non-modal sheets on the cdk overlay layer + @rivetjs/cdk/sheet-motion.
Calendar: month grid with navigation, cells, indicators and the year picker parts.

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: children
members.doc: Content; a function (not lazy JSX) is reactive content, rendered in a binding (e.g. a context-provided `children: () => title`).

members.name: level
members.doc: The heading level.

members.name: r:slot
members.doc: Usage side of a named slot: this element becomes the parent component's `name` slot content.

members.name: render
members.doc: Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function; spread the received props onto the element you render.

members.name: slot
members.doc:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent component.
An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all props received from a parent.
Read once at mount (it picks the context props).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: children
members.doc: The children of the component. A function may be provided to alter the children based on component state.

members.name: class
members.doc: The CSS class of the element. A function may be provided to compute the class based on component state.

members.name: defaultOpen
members.doc: Whether the overlay is open by default (uncontrolled).

members.name: isDismissable
members.doc:
Whether to close the alert dialog when the user interacts outside it.
Alert dialogs typically require explicit action, so this defaults to false.

members.name: isEntering
members.doc: Whether the modal is currently performing an entry animation (a value or an accessor).

members.name: isExiting
members.doc: Whether the modal is currently performing an exit animation (a value or an accessor).

members.name: isKeyboardDismissDisabled
members.doc:
Whether pressing the escape key to close the modal should be disabled.
Alert dialogs typically require explicit action, so this defaults to true.

members.name: isOpen
members.doc: Whether the overlay is open (controlled): a plain value, a two-way Signal, or a read-only accessor (never written: dismissing only calls `onOpenChange`).

members.name: onEnter
members.doc: Callback when the modal starts entering. Return a promise to indicate when the entry animation has completed.

members.name: onExit
members.doc: Callback when the modal starts exiting. Return a promise to indicate when the exit animation has completed.

members.name: onOpenChange
members.doc: Handler that is called when the overlay's open state changes (resumed pages: an inline arrow or a local function).

members.name: render
members.doc: Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function; spread the received props onto the element you render.

members.name: shouldCloseOnInteractOutside
members.doc: Filter: return true when an interaction with `element` (outside the overlay) should close it.

members.name: slot
members.doc:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent component.
An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all props received from a parent.
Read once at mount (it picks the context props).

members.name: style
members.doc: The inline style of the element. A function may be provided to compute the style based on component state.

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: color
members.doc: Color applied to child Avatars (and the overflow count) when they omit color.

members.name: max
members.doc:
Maximum number of avatar children to render.
Omit to show all children (no truncation).

members.name: overlap
members.doc:
How stacked avatars overlap visually.
- `"clip"` — crescent mask (transparent seam; no box-shadow)
- `"ring"` — solid box-shadow outline via `--background`
Has no effect when `isGrid` is true.

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: size
members.doc:
Size applied to child Avatars (and the overflow count) when they omit size.
Defaults to `md` to stay in sync with Avatar.

members.name: variant
members.doc: Variant applied to child Avatars (and the overflow count) when they omit variant.

Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: slot

A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent component.
An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all props received from a parent.
Read once at mount (it picks the context props).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: createCalendar
members.doc: Creates the display calendar system for an identifier (default: `createCalendar` of `@rivetjs/cdk/date`).

members.name: defaultValue
members.doc: Uncontrolled initial value.

members.name: granularity
members.doc: Determines the smallest unit that is displayed in the date picker. By default, this is `"day"` for dates, and `"minute"` for times.

members.name: hideTimeZone
members.doc: Whether to hide the time zone abbreviation.

members.name: hourCycle
members.doc: Whether to display the time in 12 or 24 hour format. By default, this is determined by the user's locale.

members.name: isDateUnavailable
members.doc: Callback that is called for each date of the calendar. If it returns true, then the date is unavailable.

members.name: isDisabled
members.doc: Whether the field is disabled; an accessor stays live (`ownerDisabled`).

members.name: isInvalid
members.doc: Whether the value is invalid (a value, or an accessor that stays live).

members.name: isReadOnly
members.doc: Whether the value is immutable; an accessor stays live (`ownerReadOnly`).

members.name: isRequired
members.doc: Whether a value is required; an accessor stays live (`ownerRequired`).

members.name: maxGranularity
members.doc: The maximum unit to display in the date field.

members.name: maxValue
members.doc: The maximum allowed date that a user may select.

members.name: minValue
members.doc: The minimum allowed date that a user may select.

members.name: name
members.doc: Form field name (server errors of `<Form validationErrors>` apply by it).

members.name: onChange
members.doc: Called with the new value (date object, in the calendar of the original value).

members.name: placeholderValue
members.doc: A placeholder date that influences the format of the placeholder shown when no value is selected. Defaults to today's date at midnight.

members.name: render
members.doc: Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function; spread the received props onto the element you render.

members.name: shouldForceLeadingZeros
members.doc: Whether to always show leading zeros in the month, day, and hour fields. By default, this is determined by the user's locale.

members.name: slot
members.doc:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent component.
An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all props received from a parent.
Read once at mount (it picks the context props).

members.name: style

members.name: validate
members.doc: Custom client validation of the value (a date object).

members.name: validationBehavior
members.doc:
Whether to use native HTML form validation to prevent form submission when the value is missing or
invalid, or mark the field as required or invalid via ARIA.

members.name: validationErrors

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: defaultOpen
members.doc: Whether the overlay is open by default (uncontrolled).

members.name: isDismissable
members.doc: Whether to close the drawer when the user interacts outside it.

members.name: isEntering
members.doc: Whether the modal is currently performing an entry animation (a value or an accessor).

members.name: isExiting
members.doc: Whether the modal is currently performing an exit animation (a value or an accessor).

members.name: isKeyboardDismissDisabled
members.doc: Disable closing with Escape (a value, or an accessor read at key time).

members.name: isOpen
members.doc: Whether the overlay is open (controlled): a plain value, a two-way Signal, or a read-only accessor (never written: dismissing only calls `onOpenChange`).

members.name: onEnter
members.doc: Callback when the modal starts entering. Return a promise to indicate when the entry animation has completed.

members.name: onExit
members.doc: Callback when the modal starts exiting. Return a promise to indicate when the exit animation has completed.

members.name: onOpenChange
members.doc: Handler that is called when the overlay's open state changes (resumed pages: an inline arrow or a local function).

members.name: render
members.doc: Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function; spread the received props onto the element you render.

members.name: shouldCloseOnInteractOutside
members.doc: Filter: return true when an interaction with `element` (outside the overlay) should close it.

members.name: slot
members.doc:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent component.
An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all props received from a parent.
Read once at mount (it picks the context props).

members.doc: The inline style of the element. A function may be provided to compute the style based on component state.

members.doc: `trigger="hover"`: delay before opening (ms). Live (read at event time).

members.doc: Rivet: the side the drawer slides in from (read once; a `Drawer.Container` `placement` wins).

members.name: trigger
members.doc:
Rivet extension (RAC vocabulary): the interaction that opens the overlay. `"press"` (RAC) toggles on
press; `"longPress"` opens on a long press (keyboard / screen reader press still toggles); `"hover"`
opens on mouse / pen hover after `delay` and keyboard focus, with a safe area between trigger and
popover (touch keeps the press toggle); `"focus"` opens on keyboard focus (press still toggles).
Read once at mount (it picks the trigger implementation).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

This option is useful in combination with `cdkDropListSortingDisabled` to implement copying
behavior in a drop list.

members.doc:
Node or selector that will be used to determine the element to which the draggable's
position will be constrained. If a string is passed in, it'll be used as a selector that
will be matched starting from the element's parent and going up the DOM until a match
has been found.

members.doc:
Function that can be used to customize the logic of how the position of the drag item
is limited while it's being dragged. Gets called with a point containing the current position
of the user's pointer on the page, a reference to the item being dragged and its dimensions.
Should return a point describing where the item should be rendered.

Amount of milliseconds to wait after the user has put their
pointer down before starting to drag the element.

Sets the position of a `Drag` that is outside of a drop container.
Can be used to restore the element's position for a returning user.

members.doc:
The drag element is also a handle when using an alternate root (`rootElementSelector`; Angular:
`cdkDrag` + `cdkDragHandle` on one element).

members.name: lockAxis
members.doc: Locks the position of the dragged element along the specified axis.

members.name: onDropped
members.doc: Emits when the user drops the item inside a container.

members.name: onEnded
members.doc: Emits when the user stops dragging an item in the container.

members.name: onEntered
members.doc: Emits when the user has moved the item into a new container.

members.name: onExited
members.doc: Emits when the user removes the item its container by dragging it into another container.

members.name: onMoved
members.doc:
Emits as the user is dragging the item. Use with caution,
because this event will fire for every pixel that the user has dragged.

members.name: onReleased
members.doc: Emits when the user has released a drag item, before any animations have started.

members.name: onStarted
members.doc: Emits when the user starts dragging the item.

members.name: previewClass
members.doc: Class to be added to the preview element.

members.name: previewContainer
members.doc:
Configures the place into which the preview of the item will be inserted. Can be configured
globally through `DragDropConfigContext`. Possible values:
- `global` - Preview will be inserted at the bottom of the `<body>`. The advantage is that
you don't have to worry about `overflow: hidden` or `z-index`, but the item won't retain
its inherited styles.
- `parent` - Preview will be inserted into the parent of the drag item. The advantage is that
inherited styles will be preserved, but it may be clipped by `overflow: hidden` or not be
visible due to `z-index`. Furthermore, the preview is going to have an effect over selectors
like `:nth-child` and some flexbox configurations.
- `ElementLike` - Preview will be inserted into a specific element.
Same advantages and disadvantages as `parent`.

members.name: rootElementSelector
members.doc:
Selector that will be used to determine the root draggable element, starting from
the `Drag` element and going up the DOM. Passing an alternate root element is useful
when trying to enable dragging on an element that you might not have access to.

members.name: scale
members.doc:
If the parent of the dragged element has a `scale` transform, it can throw off the
positioning when the user starts dragging. Use this input to notify the CDK of the scale.

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: children
members.doc: The children of the component. A function may be provided to alter the children based on component state.

members.name: class
members.doc: The CSS class of the element. A function may be provided to compute the class based on component state.

members.name: defaultOpen
members.doc: Whether the overlay is open by default (uncontrolled).

members.name: isDismissable
members.doc: Whether to close the modal when the user interacts outside it.

members.name: isEntering
members.doc: Whether the modal is currently performing an entry animation (a value or an accessor).

members.name: isExiting
members.doc: Whether the modal is currently performing an exit animation (a value or an accessor).

members.name: isKeyboardDismissDisabled
members.doc: Disable closing with Escape (a value, or an accessor read at key time).

members.name: isOpen
members.doc: Whether the overlay is open (controlled): a plain value, a two-way Signal, or a read-only accessor (never written: dismissing only calls `onOpenChange`).

members.name: onEnter
members.doc: Callback when the modal starts entering. Return a promise to indicate when the entry animation has completed.

members.name: onExit
members.doc: Callback when the modal starts exiting. Return a promise to indicate when the exit animation has completed.

members.name: onOpenChange
members.doc: Handler that is called when the overlay's open state changes (resumed pages: an inline arrow or a local function).

members.name: render
members.doc: Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function; spread the received props onto the element you render.

members.name: shouldCloseOnInteractOutside
members.doc: Filter: return true when an interaction with `element` (outside the overlay) should close it.

members.name: slot
members.doc:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent component.
An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all props received from a parent.
Read once at mount (it picks the context props).

members.name: style
members.doc: The inline style of the element. A function may be provided to compute the style based on component state.

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: total
members.doc: Auto form: number of pages (with no children, the root renders Previous, page links with ellipses, Next).

members.doc:
Whether pressing the escape key to close the popover should be disabled.

Most popovers should not use this option. When set to true, an alternative
way to close the popover with a keyboard must be provided.

members.doc:
Whether the popover is non-modal, i.e. elements outside the popover may be
interacted with by assistive technologies.

Most popovers should not use this option as it may negatively impact the screen
reader experience. Only use with components such as combobox, which are designed
to handle this situation carefully.

members.doc:
When user interacts with the argument element outside of the popover ref,
return true if onClose should be called. This gives you a chance to filter
out interaction with elements that should not dismiss the popover.
By default, onClose will always be called on interaction outside the popover ref.

members.name: shouldSkipAnimation
members.doc:
Whether the popover should appear and disappear without an entry or exit animation. This is used by
components such as PreviewTrigger to skip animations when quickly swapping between overlays.

members.name: shouldUpdatePosition
members.doc: Whether to update the position automatically.

members.name: slot
members.doc:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent component.
An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all props received from a parent.
Read once at mount (it picks the context props).

members.doc: Rivet: a `Popover.Heading` before the content (labels the dialog).

members.name: trigger
members.doc:
The name of the component that triggered the popover. This is reflected on the element as the
`data-trigger` attribute, and can be used to provide specific styles for the popover depending on
which element triggered it.

members.name: triggerRef
members.doc:
The ref for the element which the popover positions itself with respect to.

When used within a trigger component such as DialogTrigger, MenuTrigger, Select, etc., this is set
automatically. It is only required when used standalone.

members.name: zIndex
members.doc: z-index written on the overlay (React Aria: 100000). Top-layer overlays ignore it.

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: resize
members.doc:
Update the Panel's size.

Size can be in the following formats:
- Percentage of the parent Group (0..100)
- Pixels
- Relative font units (em, rem)
- Viewport relative units (vh, vw)

ℹ️ Numeric values are assumed to be pixels.
Strings without explicit units are assumed to be percentages (0%..100%).
Percentages may also be specified as strings ending with "%" (e.g. "33%")
Pixels may also be specified as strings ending with the unit "px".
Other units should be specified as strings ending with their CSS property units (e.g. 1rem, 50vh)

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: slot
members.doc:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent component.
An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all props received from a parent.

members.name: snap
members.doc:
Rivet deviation: when the thumb snaps to a step during a pointer drag. `"release"`: free drag, the thumb
animates to the closest step on release (`@rivetjs/cdk/motion` `Motion1D`, `data-snapping`); `"drag"`: React
Aria behaviour (snaps during the drag). The value, `aria-valuenow` and `onChange` are stepped either way.

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

members.name: scrollOffset
members.doc:
The amount of offset from the bottom of your scrollable region that should trigger load more.
Uses a percentage value relative to the scroll body's client height. Load more is then
triggered when your current scroll position's distance from the bottom of the currently loaded
list of items is less than or equal to the provided value. (e.g. 1 = 100% of the scroll
region's height).

members.name: render
members.doc:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an `<a>`).
* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).

Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

* Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
* You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop as appropriate.

Rivet: applied by `dom.*` (early return before the compiled element); `renderProps` is `undefined` (as upstream).
